13	)
14	
15	// status_render.go owns the TEXT rendering of `entire-brain status`. Nothing
16	// here changes what the command computes, and in particular nothing here is
17	// reachable from --json: the machine contract is byte-identical to what it was
18	// before this file existed, and the JSON golden test enforces that.
19	//
20	// The problem it solves is that the default text report had become unreadable.
21	// On a real repository it printed forty-four "partial failure: E_MINIFIED …"
22	// lines, then the SAME forty-four files again as "blind spots", then a
23	// twenty-three-entry relation-type histogram — roughly 130 lines, of which
24	// about six carried information a person had asked for. The signal (is the
25	// backfill progressing? is the watcher alive? did a component fail?) was
26	// somewhere in the middle.
27	//
28	// So there are now two reports:
29	//
30	//   - DEFAULT: identity, the onboarding block, and a one-line health verdict.
31	//   - --verbose: everything the old report printed, except that repeated
32	//     warnings are collapsed to one line per group and no file is ever listed
33	//     twice across two sections.
34	//
35	// The grouping is not cosmetic. A repository that vendors JSON corpora is not
36	// forty-four separate problems; it is one fact ("data files are not source, and
37	// were not parsed as source") that the reader should be able to dismiss in one
38	// glance and go looking at in `doctor` if they care.
39	
40	// statusDataFileExtensions are the file types whose "not parsed as source"
41	// warning is expected rather than actionable: a JSON corpus, a lockfile, a

90	// statusBlindSpotReason shortens a provider's explanation to the clause that
91	// distinguishes it. The full sentence lives in doctor.
92	func statusBlindSpotReason(code, detail string) string {
93		detail = strings.TrimSpace(detail)
94		switch {
95		case strings.Contains(detail, "minified"):
96			return "minified/bundled"
97		case detail == "":
98			return strings.TrimSpace(code)
99		}
100		if idx := strings.Index(detail, ";"); idx > 0 {
101			detail = detail[:idx]
102		}
103		return detail
104	}

106	// groupStatusBlindSpots collapses per-file records into one group per reason,
107	// in a stable order (most files first, then code).
108	func groupStatusBlindSpots(spots []brainBlindSpot) []statusBlindSpotGroup {
109		byCode := map[string]*statusBlindSpotGroup{}
110		order := []string{}
111		for _, spot := range spots {
112			key := spot.Code + "\x00" + statusBlindSpotReason(spot.Code, spot.Detail)
113			group, ok := byCode[key]
114			if !ok {
115				group = &statusBlindSpotGroup{
116					Code:      spot.Code,
117					Reason:    statusBlindSpotReason(spot.Code, spot.Detail),
118					DataFiles: true,
119				}
120				byCode[key] = group
121				order = append(order, key)
122			}
123			group.Paths = append(group.Paths, spot.Path)
124			if !isStatusDataFile(spot.Path) {
125				group.DataFiles = false
126			}
127		}
128		groups := make([]statusBlindSpotGroup, 0, len(order))
129		for _, key := range order {
130			groups = append(groups, *byCode[key])
131		}
132		sort.SliceStable(groups, func(i, j int) bool {
133			if groups[i].Count() != groups[j].Count() {
134				return groups[i].Count() > groups[j].Count()
135			}
136			return groups[i].Code < groups[j].Code
137		})
138		return groups
139	}

167	// statusCauseWidth bounds the one-line cause so the short report stays short
168	// even when a provider hands back a paragraph-length axis detail. It counts
169	// CHARACTERS, not bytes — see truncateStatusCause.
170	const statusCauseWidth = 140
171	
172	// statusCauseEllipsis marks a cause that did not fit.
173	const statusCauseEllipsis = "..."
174	
175	// truncateStatusCause bounds a cause at statusCauseWidth runes.
176	//
177	// The general-purpose truncateString measures its budget in BYTES. For the
178	// ASCII causes this file was written against the two are the same, but a
179	// provider detail carrying a non-ASCII path, identifier or quotation mark is
180	// charged two to four bytes per character, so a perfectly short cause was cut
181	// to a third of its length. Counting runes makes the advertised width mean
182	// what it says, and cutting on a rune index can never split a character.
183	func truncateStatusCause(cause string) string {
184		if cause == "" {
185			return ""
186		}
187		runes := []rune(cause)
188		if len(runes) <= statusCauseWidth {
189			return cause
190		}
191		// The RESERVE is counted in runes too.
192		//
193		// Measuring the input in runes and the ellipsis in bytes is the same
194		// rune-versus-byte confusion this function exists to fix, just on the other
195		// operand. It happens to agree for ASCII "...", and silently
196		// over-reserves the moment the marker becomes "…" -- which is one
197		// const edit away, in a function whose entire comment is about this class
198		// of bug.
199		ellipsisWidth := utf8.RuneCountInString(statusCauseEllipsis)
200		limit := statusCauseWidth
201		suffix := ""
202		if statusCauseWidth > ellipsisWidth {
203			limit = statusCauseWidth - ellipsisWidth
204			suffix = statusCauseEllipsis
205		}
206		return string(runes[:limit]) + suffix
207	}

209	// statusHealth is the one-line verdict the short report ends on.
210	type statusHealth struct {
211		Issues   int
212		Warnings int
213		Failed   []string
214		Severity string
215		// An old layout needs the migration bridge, even when Graph is absent.
216		BrainLayoutRemedy string
217		// BrainMissing reports that this repository has no brain at all: the
218		// manifest is absent and every source is unbuilt. It is a STATE, not a
219		// problem count, which is why it cannot be folded into Issues — and why
220		// the old verdict got it exactly backwards. Nothing built means nothing
221		// broken, so every counter read zero and the first command a new user runs
222		// answered "healthy" about a brain that does not exist.
223		BrainMissing bool
224		// SemanticMissing reports that a brain exists but its manifest declares no
225		// semantic index, so `inspect code`, `query` and `brief` have nothing to
226		// read. Freshness cannot see this either: with no semantic source there is
227		// no freshness report, and brainStatusFreshnessSeverity returns "" — which
228		// Healthy() used to accept as "fine".
229		SemanticMissing bool
230		// Cause names WHICH axis is not current, in the words `overview` uses. See
231		// statusFreshnessCause.
232		Cause string
233		// HostCLIMissing reports that the Entire CLI this plugin runs under is not
234		// installed. Sessions, the semantic index and the entity index are all built
235		// THROUGH it, so while it is absent no refresh brings any of them back and
236		// the verdict must say so rather than naming a command that cannot repair
237		// what it just listed.
238		HostCLIMissing bool
239		// SemanticProviderAbsent reports that the semantic index is missing AND
240		// the host CLI cannot launch a graph provider, so the refresh remedy alone
241		// cannot build it — the honest next step is the plugin install. Set only
242		// when the host CLI itself is present.
243		SemanticProviderAbsent bool
244		// SemanticStoreUnsupported reports that a graph provider IS installed but
245		// predates the read-only store contract (graph_store.go), so no refresh,
246		// commit, or stash builds the semantic index — the only remedy is the
247		// Graph upgrade. Without this flag the dirty-tree override below claimed
248		// "commit or stash" as the fix for a failure committing cannot touch.
249		SemanticStoreUnsupported bool
250		// DirtyWorktree reports uncommitted changes in the working tree. Both stages
251		// `refresh --agent none` would rebuild REFUSE that state by design — seed
252		// with "dirty_worktree: refusing to seed uncommitted content without
253		// --worktree", semantic with the same refusal to index it — so recommending
254		// that command to a reader with a dirty tree is recommending an exit 1.
255		DirtyWorktree bool
256		// NoCapturedSessions reports the session export failing because Entire has
257		// no readable checkpoints — the state every repository is in between
258		// `entire enable` and its first finished agent session. `refresh --agent
259		// none` re-runs that same export as its FIRST stage and aborts on the same
260		// error, so naming it here hands the reader a remedy that reproduces the
261		// condition it is supposed to clear. The remedy is a finished session, and
262		// setupNoSessionsHint is where that sentence already lives.
263		NoCapturedSessions bool
264	}
265	
266	// statusRemedyRefresh is the deterministic rebuild. Named, because it is also
267	// the ONE remedy a dirty working tree invalidates, and the override has to be
268	// scoped to exactly it: a dirty tree does not change the right answer for a
269	// brain that was never built (`setup`) or for a corrupt store (`doctor`).
270	const statusRemedyRefresh = "refresh --agent none"
271	
272	// buildStatusHealth counts everything a reader would call a problem.
273	func buildStatusHealth(report brainStatusReport) statusHealth {
274		health := statusHealth{
275			Issues:   len(report.Issues),
276			Warnings: len(report.Warnings) + len(report.Live.Warnings),
277			Severity: brainStatusFreshnessSeverity(report),
278			// "absent" is inspectBrainManifestHealth's own word for a brain that
279			// was never built (and for one just removed by `reset --force`).
280			BrainMissing: report.Brain.ManifestState == "absent",
281			Cause:        statusFreshnessCause(report),
282		}
283		for _, issue := range report.Issues {
284			if issue.Kind == "brain_layout" {
285				health.BrainLayoutRemedy = issue.Action
286				break
287			}
288		}
289		// Only one of the two: "no brain" already implies "no semantic index", and
290		// a verdict that said both would be reporting one fact twice.
291		health.SemanticMissing = !health.BrainMissing && report.Semantic == nil
292		// Probe only in the state the answer changes: a missing semantic index is
293		// repaired by refresh when a provider is installed and by the plugin
294		// install when none is. With no `entire` on PATH the install hint would be
295		// unfollowable, so HostCLIMissing keeps owning that message.
296		health.SemanticProviderAbsent = health.SemanticMissing && hostCLIOnPath() && !semanticProviderOnHost()
297		if report.Onboarding != nil {
298			health.HostCLIMissing = report.Onboarding.HostCLIMissing
299			for _, component := range report.Onboarding.Components {
300				// Matched on the persisted detail, not the state: new records say
301				// "skipped", but a record written by an older build still says
302				// "failed" for the same condition, and both need the same remedy.
303				if component.Name == brainComponentSemantic && setupIsGraphStoreUnsupported(component.Detail) {
304					health.SemanticStoreUnsupported = true
305				}
306				if component.State == "failed" {
307					health.Failed = append(health.Failed, component.Name)
308					if setupIsNoReadableSessions(component.Detail) {
309						health.NoCapturedSessions = true
310					}
311				}
312			}
313		}
314		// The live worktree, not a freshness axis. The `dirty-unindexed` axis is one
315		// SYMPTOM of a dirty tree and it was the obvious thing to key on, but it is
316		// not the condition: after `refresh --worktree` the seed axis reads
317		// `dirty-indexed` and freshness aggregates to "ok", while `refresh --agent
318		// none` goes on refusing to reseed the same uncommitted content. Asking the
319		// working tree directly covers both.
320		health.DirtyWorktree = report.Live.Dirty
321		return health
322	}

324	// statusFreshnessCause is the store-validity signal, and it is the SAME one
325	// `overview` prints: semanticStaleReport opens the semantic SQLite store and
326	// runs `PRAGMA integrity_check` on it, records the failure as
327	// store=unsafe (…), and freshnessSummary renders that axis. `overview` calls
328	// freshnessSummary; the short status report kept only the aggregate severity
329	// and threw the axes away, so one shredded SQLite file, a semantic index one
330	// commit behind, and a provider that was skipped all printed the same single
331	// word.
332	func statusFreshnessCause(report brainStatusReport) string {
333		parts := make([]string, 0, 2)
334		for _, freshness := range []*staleReport{
335			semanticFreshnessOf(report),
336			retrievalFreshnessOf(report),
337		} {
338			if freshness == nil || freshness.Severity == "ok" {
339				continue
340			}
341			if summary := freshnessSummary(*freshness); summary != "" {
342				parts = append(parts, summary)
343			}
344		}
345		return truncateStatusCause(strings.Join(parts, "; "))
346	}
347	
348	func semanticFreshnessOf(report brainStatusReport) *staleReport {
349		if report.Semantic == nil {
350			return nil
351		}
352		return report.Semantic.Freshness
353	}
354	
355	func retrievalFreshnessOf(report brainStatusReport) *staleReport {
356		if report.Retrieval == nil {
357			return nil
358		}
359		return report.Retrieval.Freshness
360	}

362	// Total is how many distinct problems the verdict is reporting.
363	func (h statusHealth) Total() int { return h.Issues + h.Warnings + len(h.Failed) }
364	
365	// Healthy reports whether the verdict is "nothing to do". A degraded or unsafe
366	// freshness severity counts as unhealthy even with no issues: a stale index is
367	// the failure most likely to make the brain quietly wrong. An absent brain and
368	// an absent semantic index are never healthy either — they are the two states
369	// in which every counter reads zero because nothing was ever built.
370	func (h statusHealth) Healthy() bool {
371		if h.BrainMissing || h.SemanticMissing {
372			return false
373		}
374		return h.Total() == 0 && (h.Severity == "" || h.Severity == "ok")
375	}

377	// repairCommand selects the subcommand that can repair or diagnose this state.
378	func (h statusHealth) repairCommand() string {
379		switch {
380		case h.BrainMissing:
381			return "setup"
382		case h.SemanticMissing, h.Severity != "" && h.Severity != "ok":
383			// Deterministic and token-free: the index is rebuilt without asking an
384			// agent for anything, which is what a stale, missing or corrupt index
385			// needs.
386			return statusRemedyRefresh
387		default:
388			return "doctor"
389		}
390	}

392	// nextStepMessage gives one actionable next step. Missing brain and blocked
393	// repair take precedence; diagnosed faults outrank a missing-host advisory.
394	func (h statusHealth) nextStepMessage(brainCmd string) string {
395		brainCmd = base.SetupBrainCommand(brainCmd)
396		command := "run `" + brainCmd + " " + h.repairCommand() + "`"
397		switch {
398		case h.BrainLayoutRemedy != "":
399			return h.BrainLayoutRemedy
400		case h.BrainMissing:
401			return command
402		case h.SemanticMissing && h.SemanticProviderAbsent:
403			// Refresh cannot build what no installed provider produces; naming it
404			// anyway sends the reader through an exit that changes nothing.
405			return "the graph provider is not installed, so code context queries are skipped; install it with `entire plugin install graph`, then run `" + brainCmd + " " + base.SemanticIndexVerb + "`"
406		case h.SemanticMissing && h.SemanticStoreUnsupported:
407			// Same shape as the provider-absent case above, and it must outrank
408			// the dirty-tree override below: neither refresh nor a commit builds
409			// a store the installed Graph cannot produce, and pairing "semantic
410			// failed" with "commit or stash" was exactly the misattribution this
411			// case removes. The dirty tree, when present, still states its cause
412			// on the line underneath (statusFreshnessCause).
413			return setupGraphStoreUnsupportedHint(brainCmd)
414		case h.DirtyWorktree && h.repairCommand() == statusRemedyRefresh:
415			// The ONE remedy resolver for a dirty tree. Line() prints h.Cause
416			// directly underneath this, and the cause used to carry a SECOND,
417			// contradictory remedy of its own ("refresh with --worktree to include
418			// current changes"). Causes state causes; this resolver owns the
419			// remedy, and it names both ways out so neither has to be discovered
420			// elsewhere.
421			return setupDirtyWorktreeHint(brainCmd)
422		case h.NoCapturedSessions && h.repairCommand() == statusRemedyRefresh:
423			// Same shape as the dirty-tree override and scoped the same way: the
424			// ONE remedy a failed session export invalidates is the one whose first
425			// stage IS that export.
426			return setupNoSessionsHint(brainCmd)
427		case h.Issues > 0 || h.Severity != "" && h.Severity != "ok":
428			return command
429		case h.HostCLIMissing && len(h.Failed) > 0:
430			return "`" + entireBinaryName + "` is not on PATH; install the Entire CLI, then run `" + brainCmd + " setup`"
431		default:
432			return command
433		}
434	}

436	// Line renders the verdict.
437	func (h statusHealth) Line(render *tui.Renderer, brainCmd string) string {
438		brainCmd = base.SetupBrainCommand(brainCmd)
439		if h.Healthy() {
440			return render.Mark(tui.MarkDone) + " " + render.PhasePaint(tui.PhaseDone, "healthy")
441		}
442		parts := make([]string, 0, 6)
443		if h.BrainMissing {
444			parts = append(parts, "no brain for this repo yet")
445		}
446		if h.SemanticMissing {
447			parts = append(parts, "no code index")
448		}
449		if len(h.Failed) > 0 {
450			parts = append(parts, fmt.Sprintf("%s failed", strings.Join(h.Failed, ", ")))
451		}
452		if h.Issues > 0 {
453			parts = append(parts, fmt.Sprintf("%d %s", h.Issues, plural(h.Issues, "issue")))
454		}
455		if h.Warnings > 0 {
456			parts = append(parts, fmt.Sprintf("%d %s", h.Warnings, plural(h.Warnings, "warning")))
457		}
458		if h.Severity != "" && h.Severity != "ok" {
459			parts = append(parts, "freshness "+h.Severity)
460		}
461		phase := tui.PhaseSkipped
462		mark := tui.MarkSkipped
463		if len(h.Failed) > 0 || h.Severity == "unsafe" {
464			phase = tui.PhaseFailed
465			mark = tui.MarkFailed
466		}
467		line := render.Mark(mark) + " " + render.PhasePaint(phase, strings.Join(parts, ", ")) +
468			render.Dim(" "+render.Dash()+" "+h.nextStepMessage(brainCmd))
469		if h.Cause != "" {
470			line += "\n  " + render.Dim(h.Cause)
471		}
472		return line
473	}

482	// statusFactsIdentity renders the fact count on the identity line. A bare
483	// "5 facts" is the manifest's CLAIM, and printing it unqualified is how a
484	// brain that had lost a fact still said 5 while recall produced 4. When the
485	// cross-check fails, both numbers are shown so the claim can never be mistaken
486	// for an observation.
487	func statusFactsIdentity(f *brainStatusFacts) string {
488		if f.Integrity == nil || f.Integrity.OK() {
489			return fmt.Sprintf("memories: %d", f.Facts)
490		}
491		// A store that would not parse yielded no count at all, so "0 readable"
492		// would be a measurement nobody took. Say what is true: it could not be
493		// read.
494		if f.Integrity.Mode == factStoreDefectUnreadable {
495			return fmt.Sprintf("memories: %d declared, store unreadable", f.Facts)
496		}
497		return fmt.Sprintf("memories: %d declared, %d readable", f.Facts, f.Integrity.Readable)
498	}

506	// renderBrainStatusShort is the DEFAULT report: who this brain is, how far
507	// onboarding has got, and one line of verdict. Everything else is one flag away.
508	func renderBrainStatusShort(out io.Writer, render *tui.Renderer, report brainStatusReport, brainCmd string) {
509		brainCmd = base.SetupBrainCommand(brainCmd)
510		// The leading and trailing blank lines separate the report from the shell
511		// prompt on both sides. The path stays in --verbose; it is machine detail.
512		fmt.Fprintln(out)
513		fmt.Fprintf(out, "%s  %s\n",
514			render.Bold(render.PhasePaint(tui.PhaseInstant, "Brain")),
515			render.Bold(valueOrUnset(report.Repo.Key)))
516		identity := []string{"manifest: " + report.Brain.ManifestState}
517		if s := report.Semantic; s != nil && s.Coverage != nil {
518			identity = append(identity, fmt.Sprintf("code index: %d files, %d symbols", s.Coverage.Files, s.Coverage.Symbols))
519		}
520		if f := report.Facts; f != nil {
521			if report.Integrity == "not_checked" {
522				identity = append(identity, fmt.Sprintf("memories: %d declared", f.Facts))
523			} else {
524				identity = append(identity, statusFactsIdentity(f))
525			}
526		}
527		if h := report.Hosted; h != nil {
528			identity = append(identity, "Brainstore: "+hostedStateLabel(h.State))
529		}
530		for _, item := range identity {
531			fmt.Fprintf(out, "  %s\n", render.Dim(item))
532		}
533	
534		if f := report.Facts; f != nil {
535			warning := ""
536			if f.Integrity != nil {
537				warning = f.Integrity.Warning()
538			} else if len(f.MissingBranches) > 0 {
539				warning = missingFactStoreWarning(f.MissingBranches)
540			}
541			if warning != "" {
542				fmt.Fprintf(out, "  %s %s\n", render.Mark(tui.MarkFailed), render.PhasePaint(tui.PhaseFailed, warning))
543			}
544		}
545	
546		// The verdict is computed BEFORE the onboarding block so the block knows
547		// which remedy the screen is already going to state. Without that, the two
548		// halves repeat each other: a dirty tree failing both seed and semantic put
549		// the same sentence on screen three times.
550		health := buildStatusHealth(report)
551		renderStatusOnboardingBlock(out, render, report, brainCmd, health.nextStepMessage(brainCmd))
552	
553		// health is already built above, deliberately before the onboarding block.
554		// main added this branch alongside a second `health :=` at this line; the
555		// declaration is dropped here rather than the one above, because the
556		// onboarding block depends on being able to read the verdict first.
557		if report.Integrity == "not_checked" && health.Healthy() {
558			fmt.Fprintf(out, "\n%s up to date\n", render.Mark(tui.MarkDone))
559		} else {
560			fmt.Fprintf(out, "\n%s\n", health.Line(render, brainCmd))
561		}
562		fmt.Fprintf(out, "%s\n", render.Dim("  `"+brainCmd+" status --verbose` for the full report"))
563		fmt.Fprintln(out)
564	}

566	// renderStatusOnboardingBlock is the part a person actually came for: is the
567	// backfill moving, is the watcher alive, did every source build.
568	// stated is the remedy the verdict will print under this block; a component
569	// hint identical to it is dropped rather than said twice.
570	func renderStatusOnboardingBlock(out io.Writer, render *tui.Renderer, report brainStatusReport, brainCmd, stated string) {
571		brainCmd = base.SetupBrainCommand(brainCmd)
572		onboarding := report.Onboarding
573		if onboarding == nil {
574			return
575		}
576		fmt.Fprintf(out, "\n%s\n", render.Bold("Onboarding"))
577		// FIRST, because it decides whether any other line is ever acted on. A
578		// brain no agent knows about reads healthy on every source and is never
579		// consulted; nothing else in this report would say so.
580		if onboarding.AgentsUnwired {
581			fmt.Fprintf(out, "  %-*s %s %s\n", statusLabelWidth, "agents",
582				render.Mark(tui.MarkFailed),
583				render.PhasePaint(tui.PhaseFailed,
584					fmt.Sprintf("not wired — run `%s setup` so your agent uses this brain", brainCmd)))
585			if len(onboarding.AgentsMissing) > 0 {
586				fmt.Fprintf(out, "  %-*s   %s\n", statusLabelWidth, "",
587					render.Dim("missing: "+strings.Join(onboarding.AgentsMissing, ", ")))
588			}
589		}
590		facts := onboarding.Facts
591		factsLine := fmt.Sprintf("  %-*s %s %s distilled",
592			statusLabelWidth, "memories",
593			render.Bar(facts.Distilled, facts.Sessions, statusBarWidth),
594			render.Ratio(facts.Distilled, facts.Sessions))
595		switch {
596		case facts.Running:
597			factsLine += render.PhasePaint(tui.PhaseBackfill, fmt.Sprintf("  (backfill running, pid %d)", facts.PID))
598		case facts.Sessions == 0:
599			factsLine += render.Dim("  (no captured sessions yet)")
600		case facts.Pending() > 0:
601			factsLine += render.Dim(fmt.Sprintf("  (%d pending)", facts.Pending()))
602		}
603		fmt.Fprintln(out, factsLine)
604	
605		daemonPhase := tui.PhaseSkipped
606		daemonMark := tui.MarkSkipped
607		if onboarding.Daemon.Running {
608			daemonPhase, daemonMark = tui.PhaseDaemon, tui.MarkDone
609		}
610		daemonLine := fmt.Sprintf("  %-*s %s %s", statusLabelWidth, "daemon",
611			render.Mark(daemonMark), render.PhasePaint(daemonPhase, describeDaemonState(onboarding.Daemon, brainCmd)))
612		if !onboarding.LastTickAt.IsZero() {
613			age := humanizeAge(report.GeneratedAt.Sub(onboarding.LastTickAt))
614			if onboarding.Daemon.Running {
615				daemonLine += render.Dim(" " + render.Bullet() + " last tick " + age + " ago")
616			} else {
617				daemonLine += render.Dim(" (last watcher tick " + age + " ago)")
618			}
619		}
620		if onboarding.Paused {
621			daemonLine += render.PhasePaint(tui.PhaseSkipped, " "+render.Bullet()+" background work: paused")
622		}
623		fmt.Fprintln(out, daemonLine)
624		// Say what the machine's ONE watcher covers. A hashed launchd label answers
625		// nothing a reader of `status` came to ask; the workspaces it is watching
626		// answer it exactly.
627		if onboarding.Daemon.Installed {
628			if coverage := describeWatchPlanCoverage(onboarding.WatchPlan); coverage != "" {
629				fmt.Fprintf(out, "  %-*s   %s\n", statusLabelWidth, "", render.Dim(coverage))
630			}
631		}
632	
633		if len(onboarding.Components) > 0 {
634			parts := make([]string, 0, len(onboarding.Components))
635			for _, component := range onboarding.Components {
636				mark := setupComponentMark(component.State)
637				phase := tui.PhaseDone
638				switch component.State {
639				case "failed":
640					phase = tui.PhaseFailed
641				case "missing":
642					phase = tui.PhaseSkipped
643				}
644				parts = append(parts, render.Mark(mark)+" "+render.PhasePaint(phase, component.Name))
645			}
646			fmt.Fprintf(out, "  %-*s %s\n", statusLabelWidth, "instant", strings.Join(parts, "  "))
647			// A row of names is not a report. Every failed component already
648			// carries the reason it failed and, for the failure modes whose error
649			// text is not actionable on its own, the hint that fixes it -- status
650			// built both and printed neither, so "x semantic" was the whole answer
651			// and the only way to learn why was to run a different command. Say it
652			// here, under the row that names it, in the same shape setup's own
653			// summary uses.
654			// One remedy, one appearance. Two components failing for the same
655			// reason -- the ordinary case for a dirty worktree, which refuses both
656			// seed and semantic -- carry the same hint, and the verdict below
657			// carries it a third time.
658			said := map[string]bool{strings.TrimSpace(stated): true}
659			for _, component := range onboarding.Components {
660				// A skipped component with a recorded reason reports too — the
661				// reason is the one thing the row's bare glyph cannot say — but
662				// with the skipped glyph and dim phase, because a designed skip
663				// rendered in failure red is the contradiction this distinguishes.
664				skippedWithReason := component.State == "skipped" && strings.TrimSpace(component.Detail) != ""
665				if component.State != "failed" && !skippedWithReason {
666					continue
667				}
668				detail := strings.TrimSpace(component.Detail)
669				if detail == "" {
670					// A failure with no recorded reason is itself worth saying:
671					// silence here would read as "no detail needed".
672					detail = "no reason recorded"
673				}
674				mark, phase := tui.MarkFailed, tui.PhaseFailed
675				if skippedWithReason {
676					mark, phase = tui.MarkSkipped, tui.PhaseSkipped
677				}
678				fmt.Fprintf(out, "  %-*s %s %s\n", statusLabelWidth, "",
679					render.Mark(mark),
680					render.PhasePaint(phase, component.Name+": "+detail))
681				if hint := strings.TrimSpace(component.Hint); hint != "" && !said[hint] {
682					said[hint] = true
683					fmt.Fprintf(out, "  %-*s   %s\n", statusLabelWidth, "", render.Dim("hint: "+hint))
684				}
685			}
686		}
687	}
688	
689	// renderStatusBlindSpotGroups prints one line per collapsed group, and (in
690	// verbose mode) the member paths for the groups that are NOT obvious data.
691	// A data-file group never enumerates: that is the whole point of the collapse,
692	// and `doctor` is where the full list lives.
693	func renderStatusBlindSpotGroups(out io.Writer, render *tui.Renderer, indent string, groups []statusBlindSpotGroup, enumerate bool, brainCmd string) {
694		for _, group := range groups {
695			phase := tui.PhaseSkipped
696			if !group.DataFiles {
697				phase = tui.PhaseFailed
698			}
699			line := group.Summary()
700			if group.DataFiles {
701				line += " " + render.Dash() + " `" + base.SetupBrainCommand(brainCmd) + " doctor` lists them"
702			}
703			fmt.Fprintf(out, "%s%s %s\n", indent, render.Mark(tui.MarkSkipped), render.PhasePaint(phase, line))
704			if !enumerate || group.DataFiles {
705				continue
706			}
707			for _, path := range group.Paths {
708				fmt.Fprintf(out, "%s  %s\n", indent, render.Dim(path))
709			}
710		}
711	}

The palette already lines up, but the structural grammar differs: the host CLI's status view uses status dots, bold text with dim separators, indented label rows, yellow warnings, and dim section rules, while the brain status command uses its own grammar of bold headers, label columns, a ramp bar, and a +/✓ component row.

Since the user wants a compact format matching the host CLI style without the multicolored bar, I'm sketching a mock that adopts that dot-and-separator grammar—identity line with repo key, manifest state, Brainstore status, then indented rows for memories distilled count, sources, and warning lines for missing code index, uninstalled daemon, and stale seed. content.text:
Recon done. Findings, then a proposed layout for your sign-off.

**What's actually going on:** `brain status` already uses `internal/tui` (same `Renderer` as setup/refresh), and since v0.2.0 the palette is literally copied from the entire CLI (`internal/tui/cli_palette.go`, `styles.go` "default" theme). What doesn't match is the **visual grammar**: the host `entire status` renders `● Enabled · branch x`, dim `·` separators, and yellow `!` warning lines — no bars, no label columns, no glyph-per-component row. Brain status instead has its own layout: an "Onboarding" block, a 14-cell red→amber→green ramp bar (`Renderer.Bar`, `internal/tui/render.go:333` — each cell is colored by position, which is the multicolored graph you're seeing), a color-ramped ratio, and a nine-item `✓ sessions ✓ seed …` row. I checked Brain recall on main: no recorded rationale ties us to the ramp bar.

**Proposed restyle of the default report** (your repo's current data), in the host CLI's grammar:

```
● Brain · gh/entireio/entire-brain
  memories 24,565 · 269/272 distilled (3 pending) · manifest current · Brainstore connected
  daemon not installed · last watcher tick 102h ago
  sources · sessions seed docs history facts patterns entities memory · missing: semantic
  ! no code index · run 'entire brain refresh --agent none'
  ! seed stale · seed and docs are based on an older commit
  Integrity not checked · 'entire brain doctor' for a deep audit · '--verbose' for the full report
```

and when healthy:

```
● Brain · gh/entireio/entire-brain
  memories 24,565 · all distilled · manifest current · Brainstore connected
  daemon running · last tick 3s ago · watching 2 workspaces
  code index · 1,204 files · 18,440 symbols
```

Key moves: the leading dot carries the verdict color (green/yellow/red) like `entire status`'s `● Enabled`; the bar and ramp-colored ratio are gone — plain count instead; the nine-glyph instant row collapses to one line that only names what's missing/failed; problems become `!` lines with their remedy inline, so the separate verdict block disappears. All the existing verdict/remedy logic (`statusHealth`) stays — this is a re-skin of `renderBrainStatusShort` only. `--json` is untouched (golden-test enforced), `--verbose` keeps its current shape, and the live refresh/setup progress bars are out of scope unless you want the ramp gone there too.

Does this layout match what you had in mind — and should the live refresh/setup bars lose the color ramp as well?

Given this is a rendering re-skin with existing tests that assert output, I should be pragmatic about process here—there's tension between the strict TDD requirement and the fact that the repo's tests already encode the expected output truth, which I'll need to update as part of this change.

I'll lean toward invoking the TDD skill to stay compliant with the strong workflow mandate, since the actual work involves rewriting renderBrainStatusShort and renderStatusOnboardingBlock along with their corresponding tests.

Before editing though, the repo guide requires a graph preflight to find callers of these functions since they're package-internal — I need to check relationships before scoping the change. Once that's done, I'll move into reviewing the existing status test files (status_render_test.go, status_truth_test.go, setup_status_output_truth_test.go, status_lightweight_test.go) to understand what assertions need updating for the new report text.

I'm now mapping out how the report fields translate into new output lines: a header with a colored status dot based on the health verdict, a facts block covering memories (with variants for backfill running, no sessions, integrity mismatches, and missing branches), a daemon status line combining state, last tick, and watch coverage, and a sources section built from the onboarding components.

For sources I'm handling built components normally while demoting missing or failed ones to warning lines, flagging unwired agents as a critical warning first, and including code index coverage, manifest state, and the hosted brainstore label when present. The warnings block collects these flagged issues plus integrity and health verdict details, deduplicated the same way the current code does, and the footer shows either a clean "up to date" confirmation or a hint pointing to the doctor command and verbose output for deeper inspection.

Now I'm figuring out that remedies should appear inline on the warning lines rather than as a separate verdict line, since the dot color and warnings already convey status. I also need a small comma-formatting helper for large numbers, consistent padding so labels like "Brainstore" align in a column, and a way to render a status dot—checking whether the existing renderer's glyph set covers this or if I need a fallback character for environments without Unicode support.

JSON output stays untouched, and I should check whether the verbose report path reuses the short renderer or dispatches separately in setup_status.go. Next I'll trace that dispatch logic along with describeDaemonState, humanizeAge, and hostedStateLabel, plus the related tests, before running a graph preflight and targeted queries.

● Brain · gh/entireio/entire-brain

input.command:
entire trail create --title "Render short brain status in the host CLI card style" --type task --body "$(cat <<'EOF'
## Why

The default `entire brain status` report used its own visual grammar — an Onboarding block, a red→amber→green ramp progress bar, a color-ramped ratio, and a nine-glyph per-source row — and read as crowded next to the host CLI's output.

## What changed

The short report now follows `entire status`'s card grammar:

- Verdict-colored dot on the header (green healthy, amber degraded, red failed); `Brain` uses the CLI accent, matching setup's terse block.
- Ramp bar and instant row removed from status: distill progress is a plain count on the Memories line; sources are one names line with `failed:`/`missing:`/`skipped:` groups. `Renderer.Bar` stays for live refresh/setup progress.
- Problems are `!` lines with the remedy inline. Dedup rules unchanged: one remedy, one appearance; failure reasons and hints still print.
- Blank lines separate header, facts, warnings, and footer.
- "Integrity not checked" moved into the short report's footer; `--verbose` keeps its trailing line.

`--json` is byte-identical; `--verbose` is otherwise unchanged.

## Validation

- Full `./internal/cli` suite green (527s), plus `internal/tui` and `internal/setupui`.
- `gofmt -l -s` and `go vet` clean.
- Golden and truth tests retargeted (`status_render_test.go`, `status_truth_test.go`, `hosted_status_test.go`, `facts_integrity_test.go`, `refresh_test.go`); the substance they pin (declared vs observed counts, one-remedy-once, failure reasons on screen, no hashed daemon label) is unchanged.

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)
EOF
)" 2>&1 | tail -10
